title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'General non-sens sur Frobenius'. This is the formal preamble for treating Frobenius structures (F-crystals, F-sheaves) at the level of topoi.

(1) Start with a square of topoi in which g: X→Y and f_X: X→X, f_Y: Y→Y are endomorphisms ('Frobenius'). The square commutes up to a given isomorphism g∘f_X ≅ f_Y∘g. Take E a sheaf (or complex) on X. Adjunction (the 'mate' of the 2-cell) gives a base change morphism c_E: f_Y^* g_* E → g_* f_X^* E, i.e. (1.1).
- Grothendieck first wrote that this needs 'degree conditions', then struck that out. The deletion is correct: the mate always exists.
- Suppose E carries a Frobenius structure F_E: f_X^*E → E (1.2). Composing gives g_*(F_E)∘c_E: f_Y^* g_*E → g_*E (1.3).
- So direct image carries objects with Frobenius to objects with Frobenius. This does not require c_E to be an isomorphism, and the direction 'f^*E → E' is exactly what makes this work.
- If E is a sheaf of groups and F_E a group homomorphism, then (1.3) is one too, since (1.1) is. Analogous facts hold in the derived category (Rg_*).

For inverse images: given G on Y, there is a canonical isomorphism c^G: f_X^* g^* G ≅ g^* f_Y^* G (1.4). Given F_G: f_Y^*G → G (1.5), one gets g^*(F_G)∘c^G: f_X^* g^*G → g^*G (1.6, next page). So pullback also preserves F-objects.

(2) Next page: for two morphisms α, β: X' ⇉ X, Grothendieck forms the category L(α,β) of pairs (E, F_E: α^*E → β^*E), with a variant where F_E is an isomorphism.
- This is the inserter, in Cat, of the inverse-image functors.
- He asserts it is a topos, with the forgetful functor being ω^* for a morphism ω: X → L(α,β), and a canonical 2-cell ωβ → ωα.
- Universal property: morphisms L(α,β) → Y correspond to pairs (φ: X→Y, f: φβ → φα). So L(α,β) is the lax coequalizer (coinserter) of α, β in the 2-category of topoi; the iso variant is the pseudo-coequalizer.
- Taking α = Frobenius and β = id recovers the 'topos of F-objects'. With isomorphisms on X⊗F̄_q this gives Deligne's Weil sheaves.

Purpose: a functorial formalism for F-crystals in the crystalline topos (Berthelot, Deligne correspondence), where pushforward and pullback of F-objects come for free.
errors: On the next page, Homtop(L(α,β), X) should be Homtop(L(α,β), Y). Also g^*(F_G) has target g^*(G), not 'f^*(G)'.
On this page the object is called 'F' once, before being called E. This is a slip or transcription confusion.
The struck-out 'conditions de degré convenables' were indeed unnecessary: the base change mate exists for any 2-commutative square. The correction is right.

ideas.what: Base change (mate) morphism f_Y^* g_* → g_* f_X^* for a 2-commutative square of topoi, also in derived categories
ideas.modern_name: Base change morphism / mate of a 2-cell

ideas.what: Direct image of an object with Frobenius structure f^*E→E inherits a Frobenius structure via the (not necessarily invertible) base change map; same for derived Rg_*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Ogus for F-crystals; Böckle–Pink (2009) for τ-sheaves in this exact form

ideas.what: Category of pairs (E, α^*E→β^*E) for α,β: X'⇉X is a topos, with universal property of a lax coequalizer of topoi
ideas.modern_name: Coinserter / lax coequalizer in the 2-category of topoi (computed as inserter of inverse-image functors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bicolimits of topoi: Moerdijk, Johnstone (Elephant), 1980s–2000s; Weil-sheaf case: Deligne (Weil II, 1980)

missed.claim: Already in the late 1960s, Grothendieck packages 'objects with Frobenius' as a topos L(α,β): the lax (resp. pseudo) coequalizer of α, β in the 2-category of topoi, with a stated universal property. This predates the explicit treatment of bicolimits of topoi and gives a single topos-theoretic home for F-crystals, Weil sheaves and τ-sheaves.
missed.quote: Prop L(α,β) est un topos, et ω^* est le foncteur image inverse d'un morphisme de topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precedent for viewing Weil sheaves and F-sheaves as sheaves on a 'Frobenius quotient' topos. This viewpoint recurs in Weil-étale topoi and in Frobenius-quotient constructions (e.g. Fargues–Fontaine-type X/φ^Z). The attribution may be early, but the mathematics is now standard.

missed.claim: Grothendieck observes that direct image preserves F-objects because the Frobenius structure points f^*E→E, so no base change isomorphism is needed. This is the key device of Böckle–Pink's τ-sheaf theory, stated here in general topos and derived form.
missed.quote: Si donc on se donne un homomorphisme (1.2) F_E : f_X^*(E) → E on en conclut ... (1.3) g_*(F_E)∘c_E : f_Y^*(g_*(E)) → g_*(E)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor priority information. The idea is formal and was rediscovered.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly formal nonsense, as the title says. The mildly notable point is the early, general topos-theoretic coinserter L(α,β) as the 'topos of Frobenius objects', with its universal property; it anticipates later bicolimit and Weil-sheaf formalisms. However, it is routine to a modern specialist.
transcription_corrections: ': [?] donné [?] pas [?], de topos' likely reads ': à isom. donné près, de topos', meaning the square commutes up to a given isomorphism.
'Si F est un complexe de faisceaux' should be read as concerning E (the object later called E). After the deletions the text reads 'Si E est un faisceau d'un ... sur X'.
'(1.2) homomorphisme de [?]' is probably 'homomorphisme de groupes'.
The insertion reads roughly 'en (1.1) l'est' / 'car (1.1) l'est', i.e. (1.1) is a group homomorphism.
'Faits analogues pour F dans une catégorie dérivée' should be 'pour E dans une catégorie dérivée'.
In (1.4), 'f'_X' is just f_X (the prime is a stray mark).
